note: Closed variety of block NAMES a code reader acts on (FR-13). A block recorded with `waiver.py --stage <S> --block "<text>"` is normally held against the refusal that stands: one the refusal does not hold would pass nothing. The blocks below are not lines of any refusal: they are names that a reader of `stage_overrides[]` recognises, so the writer (scripts/waiver.py, `block_name_row`) accepts them whatever the standing refusal holds or when none is known, and `--remark` is no substitute (no reader reads a remark). A row: `block` - the whole text, case and spaces folded (a longer text that merely contains it is no name); a text ending in ONE `<placeholder>` is a prefix and must be followed by a non-empty value (an unfilled placeholder is no value); `reader` - `<module>:<function>` of scripts/, the code that recognises the name (a reader that is no function of scripts/ is refused by the loader, naming the row; a method is written `<module>:<Class>.<method>` - the class must stand at column 0 of the module and the method be defined inside its body, any other shape is refused); `stages` - the stage ids the name is read at, or `*` for every stage; an optional `class` - a non-empty string: the record of this name is stored with it, and a reader of the class (`contract.probe_gap_class_word`) takes that word as the person's answer for every instance of the class. A text that is not here is a line of a refusal and is held against the record as before. A table that cannot be read, or holds a bad row, makes the writer refuse the block and name this file: never a pass.
